reply_text:
I found one dated AI prediction from Sam Altman in 2020, and it's a borderline case. Two other items didn't make the bar.

**The candidate.** At Rescale's Big Compute conference in San Francisco (February 11–12, 2020), Rescale's official transcript records Altman saying that the computing power used to train the biggest AI models "has been growing about 8x per year for about eight years now. And I think it's gonna keep going like that for about five years." You should decide whether it counts. It's about how big AI models can get across the whole field, not about any company's spending. But it's close to the "chips/data-centre" category you exclude.

**Not included:**
- In the same talk he said "we are going to see an explosion in the next few years" of language AI. "A few years" has no date and isn't about when AGI arrives, so I left it out.
- In the October 2020 Exponential View podcast with Azeem Azhar, he said GPT-3 "is not AGI" and does not mean "AGI is around the corner". That's an undated remark on AGI timing, so it goes under undated. I read it in HBR's transcript of the 2023 rerun, which plays the 2020 recording. HBR's original 2020 episode page has no transcript, and I didn't open Exponential View's members-only transcript.
- His July 2020 "The GPT-3 hype is way too much" tweet showed up only in search snippets. I didn't open it, so I haven't quoted it, and it has no date anyway.
- I found no AI predictions in his 2020 blog posts. That source still has gaps.

**Other years.** The Peter Diamandis podcast with a "10 years from now, we'll be talking to AI" segment was filmed in early 2021, according to the page. The "by 2030" tweet about costs falling toward zero is from 2021.

I used 9 of 12 searches and 4 of 6 page openings.
